raw_text: Chinese hackers targeted Indian power grid amid border standoff: Report. A China-linked hacking group targeted at least 10 organisations in India's power sector during the military standoff along the Line of Actual Control in Ladakh, a U.S.-based cybersecurity firm has reported. Recorded Future said the group, which it calls RedEcho, used sophisticated malware known as ShadowPad to infiltrate India's Regional Load Despatch Centres that manage the national power grid. The revelation comes amid speculation that an October 2020 power grid failure in Mumbai may have been caused by a Chinese cyberattack, though no definitive link has been established. India's Power Ministry said it is aware of the report and has taken steps to secure critical infrastructure.
